candidate_evidence.quote: O6BG is a low molecular-weight purine analog which selectively and irreversibly inactivates the DNA-repair enzyme, O6- alkylguanine DNA-alkyltransferase.
Chemotherapy drugs, such as 6-benzylguanine, temozolomide, and carmustine, work in different ways to stop the growth of tumor cells, either by killing the cells, by stopping them from dividing.

candidate_flag.reason: O6-benzylguanine is the only non-established drug; it acts as an MGMT-inactivating chemosensitiser for temozolomide/carmustine, which could be read as enabling another agent rather than a candidate with its own antitumour role.

coder_notes: Single-arm trial: BG + dose-escalated TMZ (and carmustine) with P140K-MGMT gene-modified HSC chemoprotection; RT without concomitant TMZ. TMZ and carmustine coded established_therapy_experiment because the regimen alters their dose/schedule (dose escalation enabled by HSC protection); soc_backbone is an alternative ('Followed by SOC chemotherapy' in arm label). O6-benzylguanine has no INN in the record; development name used. MGMT unmethylated requirement is candidate-matched under the manual's MGMT-targeting exception. Arm label mentions 'both arms' in RT description but only one arm is registered.
